body:
Split into focused follow-ups:

- https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issues/10 — Model Breakdown tool scope/filtering.
- https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issues/11 — broader chart/tool/model/legend interaction model.

Design recommendation: make this an intentional **industrial terminal cockpit** theme system, not a generic SaaS light/dark pass.

Dark mode should preserve the current graphite terminal feel with sharper source accents. Light mode should use warm paper/porcelain surfaces with graphite text, still technical and compact, not plain white cards.

Implementation notes:

- Use semantic CSS tokens for surfaces, text, borders, shadows, chart grid, and interaction states.
- Keep tool/source colors separate from theme surface tokens, e.g. OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes accents.
- Apply `data-theme="light"` / `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`.
- Default to `prefers-color-scheme` when no user choice exists.
- Persist explicit user choice in `localStorage`.
- Add an accessible toggle with `aria-pressed` and explicit labels such as `Switch to light mode` / `Switch to dark mode`.
- Update `color-scheme` and `<meta name="theme-color">` for the active theme.
- Verify dashboard and settings page, including chart, tables, tooltips, focus states, source cards, buttons, and form controls.
- Keep source-provenance wording and API/data contracts unchanged.

Visual direction:

- Dark: deep graphite, ink-black panels, cyan/amber/yellow tool accents, subtle grid/noise texture.
- Light: warm paper/porcelain background, graphite text, muted cyan/amber accents, instrument-panel cards rather than flat white SaaS cards.
- Chart gridlines, legends, tooltip surfaces, and muted text should be tuned separately per theme.

Suggested acceptance criteria additions:

- Theme choice persists across reloads.
- System preference is respected before user selection.
- Both themes meet readable contrast for cards, tables, charts, buttons, inputs, tooltips, and focus states.
- Chart and tool-source colors remain distinguishable in both themes.
- Browser smoke covers both themes with active OpenCode, Codex CLI, and Hermes source cards.
- Existing tests pass.

Additional scope from the live `gpt-5.5` review:

- Distinguish **API-equivalent estimate** from **actual subscription spend**. A ChatGPT Pro subscription, OpenAI API key, OpenRouter key, and provider/account-specific billing can have different economics even for the same underlying model.
- Treat coding-agent harnesses separately from model providers. Example: Hermes may run `gpt-5.5` through an OpenAI/Codex provider path, so pricing should resolve through the provider/model, not through the Hermes tool name.
- Add a pricing/billing basis field that can distinguish at least:
  - public API/OpenRouter estimate
  - provider/account/API-key-specific price
  - session-reported actual/estimated cost
  - subscription-included or subscription-unknown
  - unpriced/unmapped
- For subscription-backed use, avoid presenting public API token pricing as the user's actual bill. The UI should say `API-equivalent estimate` unless actual provider billing is confirmed.

## Current Review Note
PR 22 surfaced a loading-state preference that should stay out of the token-card PR: loading affordances should be local to the affected card/section, not a full-screen or page-wide sweep.

## Clarified Loading Direction
- Cards: if cards reload, loading should be clipped inside each card.
- Chart: should have a chart-local loading state/skeleton instead of only a text note or blank redraw.
- Tables: model/history tables should use table-local loading rows/states.
- No full-page shimmer/sweep unless the whole page is intentionally blocked.

## Out of Scope
This issue should standardize UX states. Actual endpoint latency/performance optimization should be tracked separately so it can include timing, SQL/query profiling, caching, and API aggregation changes.

## UX Alternatives To Choose From

These keep the mechanic simple while giving the update action a clear product feel instead of a generic admin button.

### Option A: Footer Utility Chip

**Tone:** industrial/utilitarian, compact, command-center style.

Place a small status chip in the existing footer beside `active sources` and `last updated`.

Example copy:

```text
app: main@a1b2c3d clean · Update App
```

Interaction:

- `Update App` is a compact button/chip.
- Click opens a tiny confirmation popover: `Pull latest and sync dependencies?`
- Running state: `Updating...`
- Success: `Updated to d4e5f6a. Restart required.`
- Dirty state: `Local changes detected. Update manually.`

Pros:

- Smallest UI change.
- Keeps update near operational status metadata.
- Least visual noise on the dashboard.

Cons:

- Easy to miss.
- Footer can become dense on mobile.

Best if we want the safest first iteration.

### Option B: Settings Maintenance Card

**Tone:** refined/minimal, deliberate admin control.

Add a `Maintenance` card to `/settings` with version details and the update action.

Example layout:

```text
Maintenance
Current version  main@a1b2c3d
Worktree         clean
Upstream         origin/main

[Update App]
```

Interaction:

- Button runs the update endpoint directly after a short confirmation.
- Result appears inside the card as a persistent status line.
- Include fallback command on failure: `git pull --ff-only && uv sync`.

Pros:

- Cleanest information architecture.
- Keeps risky actions away from the main analytics dashboard.
- Easier to make accessible and readable.

Cons:

- One extra click to reach it.
- Less discoverable than footer placement.

Best if we want the most maintainable UX.

### Option C: Header Status Rail

**Tone:** dashboard cockpit, slightly more prominent.

Add a thin app status rail above the Overview title.

Example copy:

```text
Dashboard build main@a1b2c3d · clean · last checked 2m ago     [Update]
```

Interaction:

- `Update` button stays visible near the top.
- When update starts, the rail expands into an inline progress/status row.
- Success keeps the status visible until page refresh: `Restart dashboard to activate latest version.`

Pros:

- Very discoverable.
- Makes version provenance explicit.
- Good place for future app-health status if needed.

Cons:

- Adds visual weight to the main dashboard.
- Slightly broader UI change.

Best if version/update status should be part of the dashboard’s main operational story.

### Option D: Command Palette Style Modal

**Tone:** retro-terminal/operator console.

Use a small `Update App` button in Settings or footer, but clicking opens a command-style modal.

Example modal:

```text
> update app
Checking worktree... clean
Pulling origin/main... fast-forward only
Syncing uv environment...
Restart required
```

Interaction:

- Shows command phases as read-only log lines.
- Keeps raw output collapsed behind `Show details`.
- Escape closes only after completion/failure.

Pros:

- Memorable and on-brand for local developer tooling.
- Makes the mechanic transparent without feeling like a generic toast.
- Useful for debugging failures.

Cons:

- More UI code than needed for v1.
- Modal behavior needs careful keyboard/focus handling.

Best if we want a distinctive experience and are okay with slightly more implementation effort.

## Recommendation

Start with **Option B: Settings Maintenance Card**.

It is the best balance of simple, safe, and clear. This is a potentially risky local operation, so it belongs in Settings rather than competing with usage analytics. If we want more discoverability later, add a small footer version chip that links to the Settings card.

## Suggested V1 Decision

Implement:

- Settings `Maintenance` card.
- `GET /api/app-version` on Settings page load.
- `POST /api/update` from the card.
- Conservative states: clean, dirty, updating, success, already-current, failed.
- No auto-restart.

Defer:

- Modal command log.
- Header rail.
- Background scheduled update checks.
- Branch switching or auto-stash.

## Visual Mockups

I added SVG mockups for the four UX alternatives on branch `issue-34-update-ux-visuals` and embedded them below for selection.

Contact sheet HTML:

https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/blob/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/index.html

### Option A: Footer Utility Chip

Compact, operational, lowest UI footprint.

![Option A: Footer Utility Chip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/option-a-footer-chip.svg)

### Option B: Settings Maintenance Card

Recommended for v1: safest information architecture and easiest to keep accessible.

![Option B: Settings Maintenance Card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/option-b-settings-maintenance-card.svg)

### Option C: Header Status Rail

Most discoverable, but adds more visual weight to the main dashboard.

![Option C: Header Status Rail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/option-c-header-status-rail.svg)

### Option D: Command Palette Modal

Most distinctive and transparent, but more UI work for v1.

![Option D: Command Palette Modal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/option-d-command-modal.svg)

Recommendation remains **Option B** for first implementation, with Option A as a later discoverability enhancement if needed.

## UX Decision: Option B, Aligned With Current Settings UI

Selected direction: **Option B: Settings Maintenance Card**.

Important adjustment: implement it using the current `/settings` page style, not the earlier conceptual sidebar mockup.

Updated visual:

![Selected Option B: current Settings UI aligned](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/option-b-current-settings-aligned.svg)

Implementation alignment:

- Keep `/settings` as the existing centered, narrow page (`max-width: 640px`).
- Reuse the existing `.card` pattern: `#111315` background, `#272b30` border, `8px` radius, `20px` padding.
- Add a fourth card named `Application Update`.
- Do not add the dashboard sidebar or a new page shell as part of this issue.
- Keep typography, color, and spacing consistent with current `settings.html`.
- Use the existing path/code-pill treatment for the version line, e.g. `main@a1b2c3d clean`.
- Put status text inside the card, not as a global toast.
- Keep the button visually simple and consistent with the current accent color.

Proposed card content:

```text
Application Update
Update this local dashboard from the configured upstream branch.

main@a1b2c3d clean                         [Update App]

Uses git pull --ff-only and uv sync. Restart required after success.
```

State copy:

- Dirty: `Local changes detected. Update manually to avoid overwriting work.`
- Updating: `Updating...`
- Success: `Updated to <sha>. Restart the dashboard to use the latest version.`
- Already current: `Already up to date.`
- Failed: `Update failed. Run manually: git pull --ff-only && uv sync`

Contact sheet updated here:

https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/blob/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/index.html

## UX Decision Update: Put Update Control On The Homepage

Superseding the Settings-card direction.

Selected direction: **homepage top-level update control**.

Reason: `/settings` is too hidden for normal users. The update action should be visible from the main dashboard, while still looking like an operational utility rather than a primary analytics CTA.

Updated selected visual:

![Selected homepage top-level update control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/selected-homepage-top-level.svg)

Contact sheet:

https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/blob/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/index.html

## Implementation Direction

Add a compact app-version/update module in the Overview header area.

Suggested placement:

- Keep the existing `Overview` heading and subtitle on the left.
- Add a small utility card/pill on the right side of the same header row.
- On mobile, stack it below the subtitle before the date-range pills.

Suggested content:

```text
APP VERSION
main@a1b2c3d clean        [Update]
```

Behavior:

- Fetch current app state from `GET /api/app-version` on page load.
- `Update` calls `POST /api/update`.
- Disable the button while updating.
- Keep all status messages inline inside this small module.
- Do not use a global toast for v1.

State copy:

- Checking: `Checking app version...`
- Clean/current: `main@a1b2c3d clean`
- Dirty: `main@a1b2c3d dirty · update blocked`
- Updating: `Updating...`
- Success: `Updated to <sha>. Restart required.`
- Already current: `Already up to date.`
- Failed: `Update failed. Run: git pull --ff-only && uv sync`

Visual alignment with current homepage:

- Use existing dashboard dark tokens: `#0d0f11`, `#272b30`, `#38bdf8`, `#a1a1aa`.
- Match existing card radius and mono typography from `templates/index.html`.
- Make the module smaller than the stat cards so it reads as utility metadata.
- Avoid adding a new header rail or redesigning the sidebar/page shell.

Safety remains unchanged:

- Refuse dirty worktrees.
- Use `git pull --ff-only` only.
- Run `uv sync` only after successful pull.
- No auto-stash, branch switching, arbitrary commands, or auto-restart.

## Refinement: Make Homepage Update Button More Evident

Agreed: keep the control on the homepage, but use more of the original Option B emphasis so normal users notice it.

Updated selected visual:

![Selected homepage prominent update control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/selected-homepage-prominent-update.svg)

Contact sheet:

https://github.com/raychrisgdp/coding-agent-usage-dashboard/blob/issue-34-update-ux-visuals/docs/issue-34-update-ux/index.html

Updated UX direction:

- Place a compact `App Update` panel in the Overview top area.
- Make the button large enough to read as an intentional user action, not a tiny metadata chip.
- Use the stronger Option B-style treatment:
  - clear panel title: `App Update`
  - short helper copy: `Pull latest dashboard build.`
  - version/status pill: `main@a1b2c3d`
  - prominent button: `Update App`
- Keep it visually subordinate to the dashboard content, but clearly discoverable.

Implementation guidance:

- Suggested desktop size: panel around `320px` wide, button around `120px x 40px` or larger.
- Use the existing dashboard dark card styling plus accent treatment for the button.
- On mobile, stack the panel below the Overview subtitle and make the button full-width inside the panel.
- Keep update results inline in the panel.

State copy remains:

- Checking: `Checking app version...`
- Clean/current: `main@a1b2c3d clean`
- Dirty: `main@a1b2c3d dirty · update blocked`
- Updating: `Updating...`
- Success: `Updated to <sha>. Restart required.`
- Already current: `Already up to date.`
- Failed: `Update failed. Run: git pull --ff-only && uv sync`
